title: 🌍 Eryndor Living Atlas I — Continents, Habitats & Population Model
rawNotionMarkup: New Eryndor atlas layer — Year 3,847, Autumn Day 22 baseline. This is creator-requested NEW worldbuilding, not a claim that the recovered original dialogue already specified these settlements or population counts. Preserve the previously established five continents, all established peoples, Karak-Varn, the Seven independent Thrones, the Deepways, the Concord of Crowns, and the actual campaign's pause. All new figures are simulated planning estimates, not flawless censuses; the creator can amend any of them. No NPC automatically knows the full atlas, and Gloin has not travelled to these places. ## Wider urban history comparison — Constantinople, Cairo and Chinese capitals Creator's additional examples: The owner correctly raises Constantinople, Cairo and China's enormous historical capitals as further evidence that the premodern world was capable of very large cities. Fantasy population totals, including the current 22.8-million Karak-Varn model (formerly 3.8 million), are not subject to real historical population ceilings. These figures are historical scholarship analogies, not additional Eryndor populations. | Real historical city | Period | Scholarly size estimate / uncertainty | | --- | --- | --- | | Constantinople | Early sixth century; later twelfth century recovery | Often estimated at about 375,000–500,000 in the Justinianic period. Some older estimates rise toward 1 million, but the million figure is not secure; late-twelfth-century studies report at least 400,000 in some estimates. | | Cairo / Fustat | Mamluk and earlier medieval periods | Cambridge scholar Boaz Shoshan gives \~250,000–500,000 by the mid-fourteenth century, with later losses during plague; wider Cairo versus urban core and period affect estimates. One million in medieval Cairo is not reliably established. | | Tang Chang'an | Eighth century | Large premodern Asian metropolis, with some historical reconstructions around 700,000–800,000 or more, depending on whether all surrounding urban residents count; no definitive census. | | Song Kaifeng | Northern Song, roughly 1000–1126 CE | Approximately one million in Columbia University's comparative teaching material; other scholarship offers smaller values, so estimate is disputed rather than an exact fact. | | Song Hangzhou | Southern Song, 1127–1279 CE | Approximately one million in Columbia University's teaching material; other historical reconstructions also suggest around 1.1m, depending on date and district count. | Primary supporting material and scholarly context: - [Columbia University, Asia for Educators: Cities of the Song](https://afe.easia.columbia.edu/songdynasty-module/cities-new.html) — both Kaifeng and Hangzhou around a million, busy street markets, shops, restaurants, multistory houses, fire stations and charitable/public medical facilities. Columbia describes 14 fire stations and 2,000 fire-control soldiers in Kaifeng; precise local division merits source caution. - [Boaz Shoshan, Popular Culture in Medieval Cairo (Cambridge University Press), Introduction](https://assets.cambridge.org/97805214/32092/sample/9780521432092ws.pdf) — estimated Cairo 250k–500k before major plague declines; multistory Fustat dwellings, thousands of sellers, dense social stratification, and caution about travelers' exaggerated numeric comparisons. - [Anthony Kaldellis, Civic Identity and Civic Participation in Constantinople](https://www.academia.edu/80201228/_Civic_Identity_and_Civic_Participation_in_Constantinople_in_C%C3%A9dric_Br%C3%A9laz_and_Els_Rose_eds_Civic_Identity_and_Civic_Participation_in_Late_Antiquity_and_the_Early_Middle_Ages_Turnhout_Brepols_2021_Cultural_Encounters_in_Late_Antiquity_and_the_Early_Middle_Ages_v_37_93_110) — early-sixth-century growth to approximately 500k, Egyptian grain-import system and migration from many provinces. - [Koç University Byzantine Constantinople history guide](https://libguides.ku.edu.tr/byzantineconstantinople/historyofconstantinople) — maximum population estimates range widely from 250k to one million, cautioning against making a top-end speculative figure firm. - [Urban Development in China (Cambridge Journal of Regions, Economy and Society)](https://academic.oup.com/cjres/article/9/3/467/2402972) — valuable counterexample estimating Song Kaifeng around 400k circa 1000–1100, demonstrating significant methodological uncertainty. Applications to Eryndor rather than population corrections: 1. Big cities have specialized civic services: fire brigades, port inspectors, caravan brokers, public clinics, aid granaries, sanitation officers, night watches and street-repair crews; the particulars vary by kingdom and era. The precedent that Song China operated fire stations and public welfare is a stronger inspiration than portraying all medieval people as living without such institutions. 2. Busy markets really are plausible: Kaifeng's elaborate shopfronts, restaurants, markets and street traffic inspire mixed-species market districts, Guild Street, artisans and festive life. Different-size residents in Eryndor create striking architectural accommodations. 3. Administration matters: Constantinople's state-controlled grain rations and formal capital rights; Cairo's dense bazaars, property law and tax regimes; China's canals, cargo commerce and well-developed urban organizations give diverse models. Blend influences without copying a specific culture wholesale. 4. Ancient cities can endure, evolve and collapse: A thousands-year-old civilization can develop spectacular municipal institutions but also face plague, civil disorder, financial shocks, severe dynastic change and urban decline. City size does not prove every reign or institution remained unchanged for millennia. 5. Respect historical uncertainty: Differences of urban core versus metropolitan area, household counts versus head counts, and different centuries affect every estimate. Do not cite old high-end guesses as if confirmed, nor treat estimates as worldbuilding restrictions. Provenance: This is an added researched comparison in response to the owner mentioning Constantinople, Cairo and large ancient Chinese cities. Existing Eryndor places and demographics remain untouched, no in-world research has been completed by Gloin and no game time has advanced. ## Owner's creative priority and the limits of realism research Appearance does not decide possibility or success. The owner clarified: an idea that looks utterly ridiculous may work, but it may also fail. Do not veto extraordinary fantasy for Earth-based realism, and do not hand out success simply because an idea is funny or cool. Evaluate the actual circumstances within Eryndor; leave room for surprising inventions, dangerous failures, character skill, resistance and consequences. The 40K Orks reference was playful tonal shorthand, not imported mechanics. Historical research may deepen lived society—work, families, governance, food, trade, medicine, slavery, wars and culture. Do not challenge established populations, planetary conditions, moons, geography, distinctive engineering or magic merely because they diverge from Earth. The modeled population and established peoples remain as written. ## Historical urbanism reference — Rome, Londinium and Eryndor's millennia-old cities Creator priority: Real historical urban population sizes do not cap or disprove fantasy populations. In particular, Karak-Varn is currently modeled at 22.8 million; 3.8 million was the superseded baseline, and the seven Khazari Thrones and their other established populations stay intact. Eryndor's societies are often thousands of years old, with extraordinary engineering, infrastructure, magic and technological possibilities that should be allowed to develop on their own terms. Verified comparison: Ancient Rome is often estimated at 750,000–1 million inhabitants during the early Empire, with scholars disagreeing on exact numbers; one alternative scholarly estimate is around 450,000. The London Museum reports around 30,000 in Londinium by 150 CE; other historical estimates run to \~45,000–60,000, not 1 million. The creator's suggestion that a Rome surviving a few more centuries might have developed cities of 2–3 million is an interesting counterfactual, not a historically verified projection. Sources: [Cambridge Economic History, Early Roman Empire: Production](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-economic-history-of-the-grecoroman-world/early-roman-empire-production/D3F384EB636F47D422B2AC9EF2551F39); [Cambridge, Migration and the Urban Economy of Rome](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/demography-and-the-graecoroman-world/migration-and-the-urban-economy-of-rome/FD30B46CBF0A846A84E17783E4635993); [Antiquity population-method alternative](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/the-population-of-ancient-rome/BACD7DF32B0B77609CD6713B8AF88882); [London Museum, Roman London timeline](https://www.londonmuseum.org.uk/collections/london-stories/timeline-roman-london-londinium/). What history should inspire: The deeply interesting questions of how a metropolis sustains itself: food imports and farming, storage, water, sanitation, roads, ports, technical and professional guilds, taxes, housing, entertainment, bureaucracy and political stability. Roman historians show the importance of major trade networks and imported grain for Rome; Eryndor can build equivalents or invent spectacular in-world solutions. Do not turn context into a limitation: A Khazari city of 22.8m can use vast multi-level caverns, engineered Deepways, huge workshops and farms, rune-enabled systems, or other striking fantasy methods, without calculating its way down to a historical population benchmark. A civilization's millennia of history allows richer accumulated technical and social institutions; it does not require linear growth, no setbacks, or a single dynasty staying in power for thousands of years. Historical comparators are texture, never vetoes, and the Rule of Cool remains: ridiculous-looking ideas may work or fail according to the actual setting, not their appearance. ## What was already fixed before this expansion - Five continents: Avarra (Gloin's main continent), northern Tharvorn, southern Sahrad, eastern Orundel, and western Vaelora. Regions are not additional continents. - Avarra contains central Ironspine and Seven Khazari Mountain Thrones, Letharion to the west, Urakai eastward, Aldermere and Valtoria in the southwest/frontier areas, Northern Holds farther north, southern merchant routes and access toward Sahrad. - Established waters: Western, Eastern, Southern and Northern Oceans; Crown Sea; Stormward Sea; Deepwater Reaches; Sapphire Strait; Shattered Isles. Established rivers: Great Veyr, Silverflow, King's River and Sahradi River. Exact coastline and river-source positions were previously open. - Established population anchors: Khazari 24m, Eldar 18m, Urakai 31m, Karak-Varn 3.8m, and Drakari fewer than 10,000 (uncertain). Their respective states remain independent. No living mountain census exists. Aelwyn may cross the boundaries of the ordinary world and cannot be reliably counted. - Environmental and time scale (historical baseline superseded where indicated): canonical diameter 50,000 km (formerly 13,400 km); 60% water and 40% land (replaces earlier 71% ocean/29% land); 24-hour day and 360-day year divided into four 90-day seasons remain established. Sailing/land/deepway travel continues to use established daily travel ranges; teleportation and cheap general air travel are not normal. - Previously approved broad peoples: humans; Khazari, Eldar, Urakai, Drakari, Aelwyn; Halflings, Gnomes, Goblins, Ents, Centaurs, Merfolk, Giants; Wolvenkin, Foxfolk, Lionfolk, Tigerfolk, Elephantfolk, Bearfolk, Cowfolk, Pigfolk; Kobolds, Satyrs/Fauns, Pixies, Minotaurs, Brownies/Boggarts, Ogres, Trolls, Mushroom folk, Harpies. Living Mountains are their own exceedingly rare sentient category, not ordinary Giants. ## Sixfold world census is now the current baseline — 21 November 2026 Population resimulation completed: The creator explicitly accepted a 6× revision of previously simulated Year 3847 populations. The current modeled world total is 2,062.800 million residents (formerly 343.800m), with Avarra 1,019.760m, Tharvorn 171.000m, Sahrad 282.222m, Orundel 393.600m and Vaelora 196.218m. The 28-people by five-continent matrix, 133 previously quantified named settlement/Throne entries, the 18 resident categories of Bramblebridge, and the 8 other quantified patchwork places, plus habitat and carrying-capacity constraints, are audited in Eryndor Living Census XII — Sixfold Population & Carrying-Capacity Audit. Priority and supersession: All old 343.8m, 24m Khazari, 22m Seven Thrones, 18m Eldar, 31m Urakai and 3.8m Karak-Varn figures in the preserved legacy text are superseded as current demographic estimates by 6× figures. They remain intact only as historical reference or original simulation baselines. New: 144m global Khazari; 132m Seven-Throne domain subtotal included in the 144m; 22.8m Karak-Varn included in the Thrones. Do NOT add these overlapping totals. Long-lived peoples retain unchanged birth rates, and any specific community may still face housing, food, water and supply crises because the new populations are not equally concentrated. This is a historical-scale editorial resimulation, not 6× births during the current play session. No old ancient First Throne uncertain peak estimate or unnamed uncensused species is automatically multiplied. Gloin's Year 3847, Era of Crowns, Fifth Age campaign remains paused at Hadrik's desk, Autumn Day 22 \~11:25 AM. ## Dramatically expanded rural settlement and flourishing capitals — population remodeling direction Creator's latest demographic direction (21 November 2026; accepted worldbuilding direction, exact totals pending): In the substantially enlarged 50,000-km Eryndor, particularly Avarra, the absolute number of rural inhabitants and scattered villages should rise dramatically. Farmland, river basins, old road systems, highland valleys, grazing lands, woodland edges and coastal routes can support many more villages, hamlets, market towns and minor regional cities than the earlier brief atlas listed. A previously named town is one sampled example, not proof there are only a few settled places nearby. Major capitals of long-established realms should boom and flourish at roughly five- to sevenfold (or greater where justified) compared with the earlier draft population figures, subject to differentiated development, not a mandatory uniform multiplier applied to every state or settlement. The expansion describes the retconned setting's long-term scale, not a sudden population explosion during Gloin's paused campaign. Illustrative capital ranges, NOT adopted finalized censuses: Karak-Varn 3.8m old baseline × 5–7 = 19.0–26.6m; Valenor 0.860m → 4.30–6.02m; Highmere 0.510m → 2.55–3.57m; Elenvar 0.420m → 2.10–2.94m; Khurazh 0.630m → 3.15–4.41m. Some capitals and trade hubs may not fit this exact range, so individual values still require explicit creator review. New towns need ecologies, agricultural hinterlands, river systems, trade networks and governance, not ungrounded place-name proliferation. A giant capital needs food, water, sanitation, logistics, housing, energy, transport and realistic social structure within Eryndor's fantasy engineering capabilities. Critical continuity correction: The old global 343.8m population model, old worldwide Khazari 24m and old seven-Throne total 22m, and other per-people/per-continent simulated totals are now explicitly provisional baselines for demographic rebuilding. E.g., a 19–26.6m Karak-Varn alone cannot be cleanly reconciled with old 24m world Khazari or a 22m seven-Throne combined count after all their capitals also expand. This warning described the period BEFORE the accepted sixfold demographic resimulation; the new current world total is 2,062.800 million, and the old totals are archival baselines. Recalculate city, domain, people, continent, rural/urban and global population figures coherently and avoid double-counting; nothing is yet locked beyond this scale-and-distribution preference. The planet's total surface grew about 13.9-fold over the old model, while total dry-land surface grows about 19.2-fold when changing from the old 29% to 40% land assumption. These are global area ratios, not the specific Avarran land expansion ratio, nor automatic demographic multipliers. Protected canon: Prior recorded family dynamics, lifespans, ordinary physics, birth rates unchanged, social diversity, ancient histories, the independent seven Thrones, magical foundations and Gloin's exact campaign pause. Keep plenty of difficult, dangerous and genuinely uninhabited wilderness across the vast continents even alongside greatly increased rural settlement; villages and minor cities should cluster unevenly according to geography and historical development. The Veiled Inland Sea's connected but outside-isolated shore villages remain separately governed by the established concealment premise. ## Chosen five-continent distribution and population review hold — 21 November 2026 Chosen land allocation: Model 3 — The Twin Titans (creator accepted, 21 November 2026). The 50,000-km-diameter planet has 60% water and 40% land. Its total land surface is approximately 3,141.593 million km². Allocate net land area (not all areas inside continental coastal outlines) as: Avarra 32% = 1,005.310 million km²; Orundel 28% = 879.646 million km²; Tharvorn 12% = 376.991 million km²; Sahrad 12% = 376.991 million km²; Vaelora 11% = 345.575 million km²; separate islands and archipelagos 5% = 157.080 million km². These percentages sum to 100% of the planet's land, and detached island land assigned to the 5% category must not be counted again under a continental total. The inland sea's open water is water, not land. The specific coastlines, coordinates, distances, countries, trade routes and regional extent remain to be resurveyed at this scale. POPULATION REVIEW HOLD — latest creator interruption: The creator explicitly said “Hold up on population.” Do not treat the existing approx. 343.8-million global simulated total or per-continent modeled totals as settled demographics for the 50,000-km world, and do not automatically multiply them by new land area. Likewise do not silently revise or erase pre-existing local, racial or city-specific population anchors (such as Karak-Varn 3.8m and Khazari 24m). Retain prior figures as traceable earlier reference while their applicability is discussed. All proposed new population totals, densities, distributions and potential revisions are open and require further creator decisions. Existing birth rates and family dynamics are not modified by this decision; nothing changes in Gloin's campaign time or knowledge. ## Planetary satellite count — revision cross-reference The creator has established an 8.5× increase in the current moon count: previous 26–30 satellites are replaced by approximately 221–255 natural moons (working midpoint 238); exact orbital and size distributions remain open. This changes neither the five-continent land split nor the 60/40 water-land allocation or surface weather and gravity defaults. The planet's own Natural Magic remains independent of its moons. ## Finalized surface ratio — 60% water / 40% land (creator decision, 21 November 2026) Binding planetary composition: 60% water, 40% land. This supersedes all 'under consideration' 71% ocean/29% land baseline descriptions. Under the established 50,000-km planetary diameter and standard sphere area calculation, Eryndor has about 7.854 billion km² total surface, of which approximately 4.712 billion km² is water and 3.142 billion km² is land. These figures refer to surface coverage, not an in-world survey, and do not automatically allocate land to Avarra, Tharvorn, Sahrad, Orundel or Vaelora. The land allocation is now chosen as Model 3 — The Twin Titans, detailed above; previous models are rejected alternatives, not binding geography. Population applicability remains under review. Preserve all previously established populations, seven Thrones, magical rules, 24-hour days, 360-day years and Gloin's exact pause. ## Finalized diameter — 50,000 km (creator decision, 21 November 2026) Binding current-world size: Eryndor is a 50,000-km-diameter planet (radius about 25,000 km; ideal spherical circumference approximately 157,080 km). Its theoretical total surface area is about 13.9 times that of the former 13,400-km-diameter model. The old planet-size value and any old full-globe mileage or map scale bar are superseded, while earlier reference-map offsets and routes can be retained as historical planning material until resurveyed. The exact new coastlines, Avarra's share of the globe and dimensions of the other four continents remain open; the world-wide water/land ratio is now fixed at 60/40; do not proportionally scale every local road, city, household, sea or population by default. Keep the previously agreed seven Thrones and the veiled inland sea geography. Protected normality: Ground-level gravity, breathing, falling, water, weather, familiar life and common material physics should behave ordinarily except for already-established magic. A detailed planetary mass/density explanation has not been established and should not be invented. The 24-hour day, 360-day year, existing lunar magic rules, population figures and birth-rate assumptions stay unchanged, as does the paused campaign chronology. ## Eryndor planetary scale clarification — ordinary physics unchanged (21 November 2026) Creator's explicit correction: Eryndor is to become much larger and more geographically extraordinary than the earlier Earth-sized map, but its ordinary physical and biological properties still behave as they do in the familiar world. Gravity, the experience of walking and falling, liquid water, weather, atmosphere and breathing, ecology, agriculture, and everyday material and biological behaviour are not being rewritten. Extraordinary exceptions come from the already established intrinsic planetary Natural Magic, lunar magical disciplines and other deliberately defined fantasy phenomena, not a blanket change in physical laws. 'Not Earth-like' refers to its world scale, distribution of land and oceans, vast landscapes and unusual geography, not alien everyday physics. Still to choose: Continent measurements and land distribution among continents/islands, mass/density treatment and surveyed travel distances; planet diameter is now established at 50,000 km (radius approximately 25,000 km). Do not manufacture the remaining values. The earlier 13,400-km diameter, 71% water/29% land and approximate 42,000-km circumference are superseded by 50,000-km diameter, 60% water/40% land and approximately 157,080-km circumference, without invalidating normal physics. Preserve established 24-hour days, 360-day years, seasons, populations, birth rates, the Seven Thrones and the paused campaign unless directly revised. Any future large-world mass/density/gravity design must be consistent with the creator's demand for normal surface experience; no new physics mechanism is automatically established. ## Avarra settled western expansion and southeastern Urakai badlands — creator design (21 November 2026) Creator's governing geographical settlement direction: The thousands-of-miles-wide territory between Avarra's far western coastline and the Ironspine Mountains is populated with more of the existing elder peoples, at least two distinctive human cultural regions, and Urakai societies; it is NOT a blank forest, an entirely Eldar monopoly, or an empty ocean-to-mountain stretch. The eastern and southeastern badlands/wastes must also contain substantial established Urakai (orc) populations rather than portray all orcs only in the Eastern Grasslands or all badlands as uninhabited. Both directions complement, rather than replace, the already-established Eldar Letharion High Sovereign, southern Aldermere and Valtoria, and independent Eastern Grasslands Urakai clan cities. ### Expanded west — cultural geography (new placement directions) - Deep and northern Letharion: A very large connected forest domain with multiple Eldar houses, high-canopy courts, scholar groves, river-house settlements, independent woodland communities and protected old-growth country. The High Sovereign exists, but independent councils and houses do not share a single politics. Ent grove societies and Pixie settlements occupy some woods; Aelwyn Fae may maintain seasonal court enclaves and uncommon crossings, which are not automatically public cities or universally accessible lands. Aelwyn and Pixies are separate peoples, not interchangeable 'fairies'. Drakari might have rare remote court or sanctuary territories, but no mass dragon population or exact location is declared. Smaller peoples and mixed communities (Gnomes, Halflings, Goblins, Satyrs, Brownies and others) can be substantial and culturally distinctive. - Western and southwest river valleys and foothills: Broad fertile plains and wooded belts with distinct human river-farming and inland market-town cultures, mixed with Eldar, Gnomes, Halflings and other existing peoples. Some communities can be influenced by Aldermere without automatically becoming new Aldermere provinces. Freeholders, river-canal guilds, caravan market leagues and hereditary local lords may coexist; legal/political boundaries remain open. - Far-western outer coasts and storm-facing peninsulas: Another distinct human maritime/coastal cultural grouping, with navigators, seafaring town leagues, fortified ports, weather traditions, fishing and remote island contact. These can trade with the established Shattered Coast merchant republics without silently being those same republics, Valtorian colonies or a unified new empire. Include nonhuman merchant, crafts and shore settlements, and preserve the Shattered Gulf's indented southwestern coast. - Western uplands, dry western marches and road corridors: Urakai traders, herders, mixed frontier towns and some long-standing urban or mountain-edge communities must be present west of the Ironspine too; no premise confines the species to the east. They interact through markets, treaties, cultural mixing, competing land use and at times warfare, not merely as hostile raiders. Existing northern forests and wildlands still have vast stretches of genuinely difficult terrain. ### Southeastern wastes and badlands — settled Urakai homelands (new binding habitation direction) - Urakai are indigenous or long-established peoples of multiple major southeastern badlands/wastes communities; the precise prehistoric origin of any given clan remains open. They are not just occasional invaders or temporary caravans from the eastern plains. Show recognisable permanent cities/fortified towns in canyon basins, near spring-fed rivers, protected oases and volcanic/mesa foothills, plus distributed hamlets, mine towns, road stations and migrating pastoral/clan groups. Strong enough local political institutions for law, trade, sophisticated craft, engineering, agriculture and military history. - Possible regional cultures, proposed descriptive labels not confirmed state names: canyon-basin waterwardens (reservoir builders, collective cistern laws, terrace farms), ash-ridge foundry clans (ore, ceramic craft, sophisticated metalwork and severe heat safety), salt-road caravan confederations (wells, navigation, trader treaties, mobile households), and dry-grassland edge settlements (pastoral and farm links to the Eastern Grasslands). These societies can have different dialects, governments, faiths, classes, attitudes toward outsiders and rivalries; a single 'badlands orc king' or automatic warlord state is NOT canon. - Resource/carrying capacity: Most scorched and dry interior terrain remains sparse or physically uninhabited; the substantial Urakai numbers concentrate around perennial springs, river corridors, aquifers, cistern chains, crop terraces, quarry/mineral trade, livestock routes and coastal trade access. Canals, runic/ordinary engineering, storage and imports help support larger cities but cannot erase drought, conflict or bad harvests. Populations and city sizes must be determined as nested shares of the existing numerical continent/people allocation rather than added to it. - Relations: Eastern Grassland Urakai and badlands Urakai can be related or competing cultures, with migration, treaty roads and trade linking the grasslands, Ironspine east/southeast foothills and far southern regions. Some populations also interact with Valtoria and local mixed peoples. No Urakai people or Urakai-specific magic is intrinsically evil on account of ancestry; actual moral character belongs to individual actions and particular magical forces. ### Demographic, religious and cartographic guardrails Under the creator's sixfold demographic model, Avarra has 1,019.760 million modeled residents, including 108 million Avarran Urakai, 72 million Avarran Eldar, and 468 million Avarran humans. The new western and southeastern communities are distributions within these already-counted figures, not extra populations added to the continental total. Aelwyn remain uncensused in the 28-people numerical matrix; do not manufacture a precise Fae census. The settlements need many thousands of miles of viable trade, farmland and transport corridors, but climate, rocky uplands, river access and wilderness create strong settlement differences. Preserve birth rates and long-lived family dynamics. Dwarven chart requirements: On an updated private Khazari map, extend the far west with named Letharion Forest, ancient Eldar centers, Ent/Fae enclaves and smaller-peoples' woodland towns; mark two human culture belts (inland agrarian river/market societies and far-west maritime/port societies), plus some western Urakai settlements along uplands and roads. Mark several Urakai settlement clusters and substantial cities inside the southeastern badlands and wastes with trade roads following water and canyon routes. Do not move the seven Ironspine Thrones, expose the hidden Veiled Inland Sea to public maps, erase the Shattered Gulf, or replace established cultures and city names with AI-invented sovereign states. No unapproved proper names, dates, scale bars or arbitrary city population labels become canon from the illustration. In-world Gloin has not acquired an omniscient survey merely because we design one out-of-character. ## Confirmed scale preference — western coast thousands of miles from Ironspine (21 November 2026) Creator-approved continental feeling: The western coastline of Avarra should stand thousands of miles from the Ironspine Mountains across significant stretches, not just a narrow region outside the mountains. This distance and scale are now a creative geographic requirement; it makes room for a vastly larger Letharion Forest, substantial open and cultivated plains, old regional kingdoms, dispersed villages, expanding minor cities, and highly populated ancient capitals supported by enormous hinterlands. Retain strong contrasts between densely cultivated/urbanized cores and sparsely inhabited wilderness, mountain valleys, wetlands and forests. Journeys across the breadth of the continent are consequential, with realistic routes, travel times, food logistics and economic ties, not automatic two-day crossings. Precision remains open: “Thousands of miles” is a broad distance class, not yet an exact coastline-to-Ironspine mileage for every point. Do not canonize illustration scale bars, approximate roads or invented new region names, and do not scale all local roads, city populations, interior basin dimensions, or the Seven Thrones indiscriminately. The western coastal expansion, northward spread of Letharion, Shattered Gulf, Aldermere and Valtoria plains, ring-bound Veiled Inland Sea, seven throne seats and previously established populations remain intact. ## No extinctions at the Second Age-ending earthquake catastrophe; magic's protective role unresolved (creator direction, 21 November 2026) HARD CREATOR RULE — NO EXTINCTIONS: The extreme planetwide earthquakes that ended the Second Age (Year 1,437), the ancient Ironspine ring's tenfold global aftershock amplification, and the almost instantaneous violent raising of marshlands and lowlands did NOT cause the extinction of any entire race or species. Every people survived somewhere in Eryndor. This is not a minor casualty event: deaths could be enormous, the worst directly uplifted communities had no time to flee, and individual towns, districts, settlements, cultural communities and regional societies could be overwhelmed or destroyed. No entire species is wiped out. Do not introduce a vanished “last of their kind” race, extinct biological species, or world-level people extinction to dramatize the quake. Creator's developing magic idea: A magical force will play some part in the survival of the peoples and the prevention of extinction. This is an explicit direction for future worldbuilding, NOT a settled magical mechanism or fully described historical episode. Its identity, origin, capabilities, degree and manner of influence, timing, whether it acts intentionally, who knows about it, and whether it relates to Lunar Magic, the independent World's Breath, gods of magic, the Ironspine Mountains, or something else are all UNDECIDED. Do not automatically make it a global protective barrier, time reversal, immortality, a moon deity's act, or an unexplained universal resurrection. The magic's contribution must be reconciled eventually with the immense deaths and near-zero warning. This note does not establish that people understood its role at the time. Era boundary and protected gaps: This is canon about the event ending the Second Age and beginning the Third Age, now complemented by authorized histories of cultures, rulers and regional warfare in the 116-year Avarran Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437), as recorded in the Second Age Annals. The race-specific Awakening (Years 1–321) and Wonder (Years 322–1,321) histories remain intact, as do permanent losses of certain moon-specific magical disciplines (which are NOT species extinctions) caused at the end of the First Age. First Throne involvement in any Age transition is still only an optional undetermined storyline, not a factual claim. No present population census changes or new species ancestry is implied. ## Urakai / Orcs — FIRST APPEAR IN THE THIRD AGE, absent from First and Second Ages (binding creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON CHRONOLOGICAL RULE — supersedes conflicting earlier text: Urakai (Orcs) did not exist in the First Age or anywhere in the 1,437-year Second Age. The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime in the Third Age, intending first to besiege the dwarven Khazari strongholds and then to attack Eldar and human kingdoms. Their exact Third Age year, creation method, first location, first Orc communities, degree of subsequent mage control and actual military results remain UNDECIDED. No Orc inhabitants, settlements, armies or history can occur in the Second Age's Awakening (Years 1–321), Wonder (Years 322–1,321) or Fire (Years 1,322–1,437), or the First Age. Some people pursue work and family simultaneously; other individuals choose solitude, courtship later or no children. An engrossed craftsperson can be a devoted parent, grandparent, sibling or clan elder. Neither a general marriage rate nor any birth/fertility rate is being newly specified or changed. Concrete existing proof: The ordinary working-class Hammerfeld household includes father Durgan (168), mother Mara (161), and four children: Bruni (57), Gloin (42), Tovin (34) and Elska (26). This family structure and its Day 21 supper are established story canon, not newly proposed worldbuilding. Don't shrink that family, change anyone's ages, or infer absence of kinship because a Tolkien comparison discussed unmarried Dwarves. A multi-century clan may span several simultaneous generations while birth-rate assumptions remain exactly as previously established. ## Long lives can deepen interests without changing birth rates The creator established a cultural principle: many long-lived inhabitants may become thoroughly absorbed in professions, art, scholarship, possessions, engineering, private passions or other pursuits, sometimes placing them ahead of courtship and raising children. Tolkien's Dwarves provide a literary example of devotion to craft; Tolkien's Elves often have children in one phase of their lives and devote attention elsewhere later. This is inspiration rather than an imported Tolkien reproductive law, and self-absorption is not the same as selfishness or universal neglect of family. Do not change fertility or birth-rate assumptions: No adjustment to any established rate, reproductive pattern, marriage ratio or census. The already established multi-million populations of long-lived peoples remain intact. Use this only as cultural texture and plausible social variety: centuries-long apprenticeships, artistic masterpieces, long-running guild feuds, dynastic archives, professional obsession and family commitment in different combinations. See 02 — Peoples & Cultures for the fuller distinction and [Tolkien Gateway: Elven life cycle](https://tolkiengateway.net/wiki/Elven_life_cycle) and [Tolkien Gateway: Dwarves](https://tolkiengateway.net/wiki/Dwarf) for the external inspiration. ## Demographic reality and population logic - Approximate continent population: Avarra 170m; Tharvorn 28.5m; Sahrad 47m; Orundel 65.6m; Vaelora 32.7m. Oceanic Merfolk are accounted under the relevant coast rather than as an extra continent. Excluded rare peoples could add to the figure, but no confident universal total is asserted. - Settlement tiers by resident count: scattered family stead 5–40; hamlet 40–250; village 250–2,500; large village 2,500–7,000; market town 7,000–25,000; fortified town 25,000–70,000; regional city 70,000–300,000; major capital 300,000–1,000,000; extraordinary metro above 1m. Population thresholds refer to local residents, not armies and travellers. - World-wide modeled settlement distribution: About 72% of modeled people dwell in agricultural, fishing, woodland, steppe, nomadic or subsistence communities; about 19% in market/fortified towns and small cities; about 9% in major cities and continuous metro belts. Khazari are an exception due to huge multi-cavern underground metros; their food, water, ventilation, sanitation, access gates and imported produce must be budgeted and defended. - Population change: Annual births, deaths, disease, migration and warfare vary. Khazari/Eldar long lives do not imply fast natural population growth; high-life-span societies tend toward low birth frequency and long training cycles. Avoid simplistic “all ancient races die out” and avoid automatic human replacement. Remote Ents, Giants, pixies and others have ecological capacity constraints; no magical limitless food. - Production constraint: A large city needs surrounding rural villages, underground agriculture, market gardens, clean water, stores, trade caravans, transport and roads. Most towns are service centers for large numbers of unlisted hamlets. The gazetteers name representative nodes, not every dwelling in 343.8m lives. - Military constraint: A reported population is not an army. Permanent armed forces require pay and grain; seasonal levies take farmers from fields. Population can influence strategic potential but logistics decide what can be sustained. - Non-human autonomy: Merfolk control or share their own undersea jurisdictions, Ents organize groves, Aelwyn operate through seasonal courts, Goblins have town councils and contracts, and mixed settlements grant real legal standing to their residents. No society is biologically mandated to be good or evil. - Unknown census: Aelwyn and Drakari populations; Living Mountains' number; uncontacted communities; exact undersea frontiers and hidden burrows; local registries disputed by border authorities. ## Population concentration and land use by continent ### Avarra (\~169.960m) - Ironspine and Deepway gate belt (\~27.5m modeled of all peoples): Khazari 22m within Seven Thrones plus border/market residents of humans, Gnomes, Goblins, Kobolds, Mushroom folk and occasional mixed travelers. Surface granaries, underground farms, waterworks and gates sustain the cities. - Letharion and western forest fringe (\~19.5m): Eldar heartland and royal-house domains, plus Halfling farmsteads, pixie canopy clusters, satyr communities, Ent groves, Gnomish scholars and woodcraft towns. - Aldermere (\~29.5m): Human grain valleys with Halfling majority pockets, Cowfolk dairies, Gnomish market workshops, Wolvenkin frontier settlements and Pigfolk riverside farms. - Valtoria and Marches (\~35.5m): Human imperial towns and grain/horse frontier, fortified river gates, traders and many mixed households; state militarisation makes iron, carts and food strategically important. - Urakai eastlands (\~30m): The largest Avarran Urakai populations with Centaurs, Goblins, Kobolds, Pigfolk and Cowfolk around open-range grain, herds, irrigation and volcanic minerals. - Northern Holds (\~13.5m): Humans, Wolvenkin, Bearfolk and Giant hinterlands, fish ports, timber halls and winter caravan shelters. - Shattered Coast republics and islands (\~11.8m): Mixed cosmopolitan ports of humans, Gnomes, Goblins, Foxfolk, Halflings, Merfolk contacts and island harpy cliffs. - Unincorporated margins and high wildlands (\~2.66m): Forests, uplands, partially settled plateaus, travelling clans and undercounted settlements. Boundaries and subregional counts are not claims about exact political censuses. ### Tharvorn (\~28.5m) Southern fjords and grain bays: humans, Goblins, Bearfolk and fishers; northern woodlands: Wolvenkin, Foxfolk, Ents, Trolls and Gnomish timber towns; inland steppe: Urakai and Centaur clans; high ranges: scattered Giants, Ogres, Harpies; nearshore shelves: Merfolk. Glacial interiors support small populations but huge unoccupied areas. ### Sahrad (\~47.037m) Sahradi river kingdoms and Sultanates: humans, Gnomes, Halflings, Pigfolk and Cowfolk; savannah: Lionfolk, Elephantfolk, Minotaurs, Urakai pastoral traders, and Centaurs; mountain valleys and oasis routes: Kobolds, Goblins, Ogres and Harpies; southern humid coast and mangroves: Tigerfolk, Mushroom folk, Pixies and Merfolk. Desert centers are clustered at water and engineered irrigation; there are wide uninhabited reaches. ### Orundel (\~65.6m) Western steppe confederations: Urakai, Centaurs, Goblins, Kobolds and Cowfolk; central rivers: humans, Pigfolk, Halflings and Gnomes; eastern rainforest and broken highlands: Tigerfolk, Elephantfolk, Satyrs, Pixies, Mushroom folk, Eldar enclaves and rare Ent groves; major sea outlets: Merfolk and Harpy cliff settlements. Do not assume eastern Urakai belong to the same warlord or central government as Avarra's Urakai. ### Vaelora (\~32.703m) Northern Elderwood forests: Eldar, Ents, Pixies, Satyrs, Brownies/Boggarts, Foxfolk and scattered humans; inland lakes: human, Halfling, Pigfolk, Bearfolk and Gnome farming/trade centers; Crownwall foothills: Khazari diaspora, Trolls, Ogres, Kobolds and highland peoples; western storm coasts: Merfolk, Harpies and ports. Many wooded interior valleys retain limited outside state contact. ## Multi-species settlement and diaspora rules - Any single people can appear outside its main range as a lawful merchant, explorer, refugee, mercenary, scholar, seafarer, migrant or individual. The distribution above is a probability and settlement map, not a hard travel restriction. - A town's resident species shares must sum to 100% for that town; visitors and caravans are separately counted. Cultures are not species; human Aldermere, Valtoria, Northern Holds, Merchant Republics and Southern Sultanates count under humans, not as additional biological populations. - Maritime accounting: Merfolk cities do not simply appear inside surface ports; have distinct submerged jurisdictions, agreed harbours, shore exchange facilities, reefs, territorial law, currents and seasonal routes. - Rare categories: Drakari territories are marked as known courts or disputed airspace, without fake census. Aelwyn court approaches obey supernatural geography and treaty obligations, not ordinary property parcels. Living Mountains are exceptional geographical life; do not place an awakening or force Gloin's relevance. - Boundary treatment: Formal land borders are drawn around tax districts and garrison jurisdictions; nomadic corridors, maritime customary rights and forest-grove territories can overlap them. Records disagree, conflict creates lived politics. ## Source provenance and future cartography This atlas was newly designed to answer the creator's request to locate all established peoples, simulate plausible demographic and material life, and support travel beyond Karak-Varn. Source baseline: 01 — World Foundations & Geography, 02 — Peoples & Cultures, 07 — Economy, Trade & Material Life. New population estimates, regional placements, basins and gazetteer names are original design additions. A drawn atlas with surveyed coordinates should be reconciled to this before declaring coordinates immutable. All settlements and populations can change as Gloin's years progress; there is no “static map” assumption.
